From: Samuel Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finasoft.com>

Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + demo: Redwood inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the initial outreach — our team is very interested in seeing Redwood in action. We were hoping to schedule a 30–45 minute demo the week of June 8. That said, I want to flag that Finasoft is entering a short spend freeze as we close the quarter and finalize FY allocations; procurement has put a hold on new purchases until the budget reset on July 1.

Would you be open to tentatively booking something for early July instead? If it helps, we could do a 20–30 minute executive overview the week of June 15 just to align stakeholders, and then a full technical demo after the budget window reopens.

Apologies for the noise — would rather be transparent about timing than keep pushing internally.

Thanks,
Sam
Samuel Jenkins
Director of ML Products
Finasoft

Hi Sam — thanks for the heads up and totally understand the timing constraints. We're happy to work around your budget window. A couple options that might work:

- Option A: Schedule a 30-minute product demo + Q&A on Tue July 6 or Wed July 7 (we can do a compact walkthrough focused on cost/latency benefits for production workloads).
- Option B: Do a 20-minute exec-level briefing the week of June 15 to align stakeholders, then the technical demo after July 1.

I attached a short demo deck and a high-level pricing summary you can share with procurement to help the FY conversations. If you prefer, we can also prepare a one-page mutual action plan with milestones (PO, pilot, security review) so procurement knows the timeline.

If you confirm a preferred date/time, I’ll send a calendar invite and include Alyssa or whoever from procurement.

Best,

Looping in a couple of quick suggestions:

- Offer a "budgetary pricing" slide during the demo that calls out Q3/FY assumptions and optional pilot discounts. Keeps procurement comfortable without committing to final terms.
- Provide a mutual action plan (one-pager) that maps dates to decisions (e.g., calendar demo, security questionnaire, PO target). I left a quick MAP template in the HubSpot deal — link below.

If we think they'll be in a hard freeze until July 1, offering a July 6 demo with a clear "non-binding pricing" caveat works well. Rishi, can you prepare a 2-slide cost/latency comparison for that session? Dev, please have a short checklist of the security artifacts procurement will likely ask for.

Thanks — Laura
